page: Microsoft Azure EC8es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at up to 4.2 GHz, backed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), alongside a large 260 MB L3 cache.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring remote premium storage volumes for data persistence. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators. Compute performance benchmarks position the instance in the top 25 percent for Geekbench single-core execution with a score of 1966.0, while multi-core workloads deliver average tier throughput, scoring 7323.0 on Geekbench and 13533.17 on PassMark CPU.

In operational benchmarks, the instance achieves 10.01 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and scores 4889.85 in PassMark database operations. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable resource efficiency for workloads bottlenecked on RAM rather than raw parallel compute cores. Because persistent local disk storage is absent, architectures must account for network storage latency when handling transactional write cycles.

Workloads best aligned with the EC8es_v6 profile include in-memory databases such as Redis, relational databases requiring dedicated buffer pools, intermediate ETL processing tasks, and enterprise caching systems.
description: Microsoft Azure EC8es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon processors on Microsoft Hyper-V. Providing 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 64.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8 GB per vCPU memory density suitable for RAM-bound applications. The architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Benchmark testing indicates strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top quartile of Geekbench results, while multi-core compute tests such as PassMark reflect steady mid-range throughput. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying on remote persistent storage for disk needs. With measured throughput reaching 10.01 million Redis SET operations per second, this instance is suited for in-memory key-value stores, relational caching tiers, and medium-scale transactional databases.
